issues.title: Large perfect HA v2: large-mode-only code paths, plan-identical guard for other templates
issues.hypothesis: q13 is the largest template (646ms, 16.6%). Its inner HASH_GROUP_BY on c_custkey (1.5M dense groups, 15M input rows) takes 2.40s CPU, the largest single operator in the profile. E0009 (perfect HA up to 22 bits, striped parallel combine, parallel source, lazy slot init, DELIM_SCAN guard) gave a consistent q13 -20..-23% over 3 runs. It was retired because the official bench showed q16 +14% and q18 +7.8%. Neither template should be able to reach the large mode: q16 groups by VARCHARs, q18's outer agg groups by VARCHAR c_name, and its IN-subquery agg on l_orderkey needs about 26 bits, which is more than 22. So the regressions were either noise or overhead that E0009 added to code shared by ALL perfect HAs, such as the refactored Combine (CombineRange/TakeAllocator) and the ScanRange source. Keeping the original code path for every non-large perfect HA, and confirming that the q16/q18 plans are unchanged, removes the second possibility.
issues.plan: Re-implement E0009 (see the ledger entry for the details: the plan_aggregate.cpp CanUsePerfectHashAggregate large mode up to 22 bits, with the density guard est_input >= slots/2, the memory guard slots*(state+1)*(threads+1) <= max_memory/8, the DELIM_SCAN subtree guard, and the threshold >= 12 guard; lazy per-slot InitializeStates; striped-lock parallel CombineRange; block-parallel ScanRange source). New requirements: (1) add an `is_large` flag on PhysicalPerfectHashAggregate, set only when total bits > perfect_ht_threshold. When the flag is false, Sink/Combine/Finalize/GetData must run the EXACT original code with no extra branches in hot loops, so dispatch once per operator rather than per row. Lazy init is used only in large mode. (2) Before benchmarking, compare EXPLAIN of every visible template against the current best. Only q13 (and possibly q02) may change operator type; q16/q18 must be byte-identical. Report this. (3) Run the bench for q13, q16, q18 and q17 at least twice each.
issues.expected_gain: q13 -20% (about -1.6% geomean); q02 small gain; all other templates unchanged by construction
issues.generality: Any GROUP BY on one or a few dense integer keys with 4K..4M groups, which is typical of FK-key aggregation such as per-customer and per-part counts. Queries with badly overestimated agg inputs could regress through memory and page faults; this is mitigated by lazy init, the density/memory guards and the DELIM guard.
issues.risk: Medium. The code is known to work from E0009. The main risk is that the official bench again flags q16/q18 noise; the plan-identity check gives the evidence to argue it is noise.

output.memory:
## Memory (gen1)

## State
- r1: E0001 JoinDependentFilterRule before DistributivityRule ACCEPTED: q19 -46%, geomean -4.2%.
- r2: E0002 contains()/LIKE length-aware selectivity ACCEPTED: q09 -37%, geomean -3.9%.
- r3: E0003 Perfect HJ RIGHT v2 ACCEPTED: q13 -18..-20%. Large range (up to 4M) only for RIGHT; for INNER it regressed q14 +52%, q18 +13%.
- r4: E0004 substring prefilter (ColumnData::Filter) RETIRED: q13 -7.7% (needed -13.8%). Good idea under the bar; retry bundled with FSST batched decode (filed r12).
- r5: E0005 BF on first key of multi-key HJ ACCEPTED: q09 -18..-22%.
- r6: E0006 join key-set range filter through compress projs ACCEPTED: q18 -6..-9%.
- r7: E0007 exact key-bitmap BF ACCEPTED: q03 -18%, q04 -20%, q09 -12%, q16 -6%, geomean -4.7%.
- r8: E0008 exact BF through CM offset RETIRED: q09 -3.9% (needed -8.6%). Don't retry alone.
- r9: E0009 large perfect HA (22 bits) + parallel combine RETIRED: q13 -20%, but q16 +14%, q18 +7.8% officially. q16/q18 cannot reach large mode (VARCHAR keys; l_orderkey needs ~26 bits), so it was noise or overhead in the shared small-HA code.
- r10: E0010 distinct HT partitioned on group hash RETIRED: q16 -7.4% (needed -7.9%). Bundle with another q16 change.
- r11: E0011 semi-join RHS-aware estimate ACCEPTED: geomean -1.6%, q02 and q18 faster.
- r12: E0012 OR-of-ranges dense-mask ExpressionFilter ACCEPTED: q19 -7..-11%, geomean -1.0%. Best 1.210x.
- r13 DISPATCHED: Large perfect HA v2. Same as E0009, but the small perfect HA keeps its original code path and EXPLAIN plans of the other templates are verified identical. If it is retired again with the same q16/q18 flags while their plans are identical, the official noise is the cause; don't retry a 3rd time.
- Claude auto-memory (~/.claude/.../memory) holds results from a PREVIOUS evolve run on this codebase/workload. Treat them as strong measured priors, not landed code.

## Profile snapshot (r12): q13 646, q18 573, q09 514, q05 267, q04 253, q17 236, q08 224, q03 201, q16 191, q07 184, q22 179, q19 170, q14 161, q02 84 ms. Geomean 239ms.
- q13 operator CPU: o_comment scan 2.72s, inner agg on c_custkey 2.40s, HJ 0.29s.
- q05: lineitem scan 0.95s, HJ 0.38s (not analysed further).

## Next candidates after r13
1. FSST batched decode + substring prefilter bundle (q13 scan 2.72s), in the backlog.
2. E0007 follow-ups: exact BF for IS NOT DISTINCT FROM (q18 RIGHT_SEMI); parallel perfect HJ build.
3. q05/q04/q17/q08/q03 not analysed yet; fresh ideas needed.
4. A bundle of E0010 with another q16 change.

## Known dead ends (prior run)
- HJ prefetch, agg run-collapse, in-place finalize, FSST heap reuse, dictionary filter, scan filter cost ordering, early HT grow, sparse perfect HJ, bitpacking select, BF on sparse perfect HJ, hashed BF through CM offset: all ~0% or worse.

## Codebase facts
- Rule registration order: src/optimizer/optimizer.cpp.
- Scan-filter cardinality: RelationStatisticsHelper::InspectTableFilter.
- ColumnData::Filter = Scan + ColumnSegment::FilterSelection (E0012's dense-mask path lives there). enable_fsst_vectors defaults to false. FSST code: src/storage/compression/fsst.cpp.
- Perfect HJ gates: perfect_hash_join_executor.cpp CanDoPerfectHashJoin; join_filter_pushdown_optimizer.cpp computes min/max.
- BF pushdown: physical_hash_join.cpp JoinFilterPushdownInfo::FinalizeFilters → PushBloomFilter; TrySetExactBloomFilter; exact fill in JoinHashTable::Finalize.
- JoinFilterPushdownColumn: include/duckdb/execution/operator/join/join_filter_pushdown.hpp. CM functions: compress_integral.cpp.
- Perfect HA: plan_aggregate.cpp CanUsePerfectHashAggregate (perfect_ht_threshold).
- Distinct agg: physical_hash_aggregate.cpp distinct_data->radix_tables; RadixPartitionedHashTable::Sink.
- Semi estimate: cardinality_estimator.cpp SEMI case (now RHS-aware after E0011). A HAVING filter directly above an aggregate already gets 0.2 selectivity as a data-source filter.
- OptionalFilter is evaluated once per row group or segment; SelectivityOptionalFilter switches off when about 30% of rows pass.
- Noise: q04/q08/q17 ±5-15%; q16 threshold ~7.9%, q18 ~5%, q13 ~14%, q09 ~8.6%. Implementer-measured gains are often 2x the official ones. The official bench can flag unrelated templates (E0009: q16/q18).
- Prior-run gains below ~10% on one template tend to fall just short officially. Prefer bundles or larger gains.
- Testing BF: compare against SET disabled_optimizers='join_filter_pushdown' on TEMP tables.
- Full profile trick: PRAGMA enable_profiling='json' + read_text + regexp_extract_all.
- Budget is tight (~$4/session): read memory/ledger tail, then dispatch quickly.
